key_insight: A recurrent automatic speech recognition (ASR) system naturally develops hierarchical representations that map onto distinct regions of the human auditory cortex, showing a parallel progression from acoustic → phonetic → lexical → semantic content across model layers and cortical sites.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether and how internal representations of modern ASR models correspond to hierarchical stages of human auditory-language processing, bridging machine representations and brain organization.
method: Collect neural recordings from human auditory cortex while subjects listened to speech and extract cortical response patterns.
Extract layer-wise activations from a recurrent ASR system and compute alignment between model activations and cortical signals using encoding/representational analyses.
Compare the content encoded at each cortical site and model layer to reveal a parallel progression of acoustic, phonetic, lexical and semantic information.
impact: Provides mechanistic evidence that ASR models can mirror human auditory-language organization, informing model interpretability and inspiring brain-constrained model design; enables cross-fertilization between neuroscience and speech-technology improvements.
visual_elements: Brain map: colored auditory cortex regions annotated with corresponding model layer indices.
Layered model schematic: stacked recurrent layers showing information flow from acoustic to semantic with example features at each stage.
Alignment heatmap: matrix of similarity/encoding scores between model layers (x-axis) and cortical sites (y-axis) highlighting diagonal/parallel structure.
Time-aligned waveform/annotation strip: speech waveform with phonetic/lexical/semantic labels above and simultaneous model & neural activation traces below.
paper_title: Parallel hierarchical encoding of linguistic representations in the human auditory cortex and recurrent automatic speech recognition systems
paper_authors: Menoua Keshishian, Gavin Mischler, Samuel Thomas, Brian Kingsbury, Stephan Bickel
